findings.title: History reads exhaust the proof-job quota
findings.scenario: The default requestsPerMinute is six; every compact request and proof job increments the same rate.count. Seven sequential historical block reads cause the seventh compact request to return 429, and six reads also deny an otherwise permitted proof submission in that minute. Each cold scan may need many more than six public block pages; the client intentionally does not retry.
findings.basis: Direct changed control flow and fixed defaults; the new test explicitly codifies cross-route quota depletion. No real cold execution inferred.
findings.requiredRepair: Keep existing proof-job quota unchanged. Account compact reads separately within the bounded client admission state, with an explicit validated read budget chosen for the intended bounded scan. Preserve trusted-proxy identity, client-map cap, connection and handler single-flight limits. Tests must show compact reads beyond six do not consume proof quota, compact exhaustion remains bounded and independently enforced, and proof requests cannot bypass their own quota.

retainedGoodProperties: Compact is default-off and only a tier may be supplied; origins derive from existing service origins.
Existing HTTP server, listener/queue shutdown and connection limits retained; no parallel lifecycle.
Fixed exact route; request query suffixes do not match. Existing browser origin and trusted-proxy address checks apply before compact forwarding.
Existing private RPC behavior unchanged. Gateway still independently captures origins/network/proofs and enforces readiness before and after fixed local upstream.
testDisposition: Five new HTTP tests unrun. The shared-quota assertion needs correction with repaired semantics; other request/response/readiness/origin/default-off assertions remain.
limitations: No source eligibility to expose the compact route until the quota defect is repaired and tests run.
Even repaired finite read quota does not establish full cold progress/capacity; the intended scan workload and recovery continuation must be checked separately.
